I woke with the smell of rain on window glass.
It had been waiting softly outside since the night before.
I opened the curtain and slowly let the gray in.
The street was empty except for a single red leaf.
It moved in thin circles, then rested against the curb.
I thought of all the small things that seem lost.
Sometimes they are not lost, merely waiting to be found.
I picked it up and held it in my palm.
Its edge was curled, brown at the tips, faintly green.
I remembered autumn from a year I could not name.
The rain stopped while I stood there, holding the leaf.
A bird sang once, then again, quietly beyond the trees.
The air smelled of wet stone, old paper, and pine.
It was not a sweet smell, but it felt honest.
I wanted to write a letter to someone I loved.
I did not know why, or if they would arrive.
Maybe love is only a way of noticing ordinary mornings.
Maybe it is the small act of keeping what falls.
I placed the leaf on my windowsill and backed away.
It looked like a soft quiet promise from the season.
The sky lightened in slow layers, gray becoming pale blue.
I made tea and watched the steam rise and curl.
For a moment, the whole day seemed possible and open.
I thought, yes, I can begin again without any apology.
The leaf stayed quietly, a small proof that mornings matter.
